notes_list.title: Carbohydrates — Classification and Fischer Projections
notes_list.basic_overview: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes, ketones or compounds that yield them on hydrolysis. Classification includes aldose/ketose, triose/tetrose/pentose/hexose and reducing/nonreducing sugars.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Glucose is an aldohexose; fructose is a ketohexose. D/L designation depends on the highest-numbered stereocenter in a Fischer projection, not on optical rotation.
notes_list.examples: D-glucose, D-fructose, ribose and sucrose are common examples.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Aqueous solution permits mutarotation through the open-chain form for reducing sugars.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: For cyclic formation, the carbonyl reacts intramolecularly with an OH to form a hemiacetal/hemiketal. Anomeric carbon formation creates α/β anomers.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Ring-chain equilibrium is rapid relative to many analytical observations; anomer ratios depend on thermodynamics and temperature.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Structural identification, stereochemistry and biomolecule chemistry.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not confuse D/L with +/− optical rotation; do not call sucrose a reducing sugar.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
